Memory-enabled support apps 2–5 use AuraDB; optional module-5 hosted workflows use a separate NAMS workspace.

notes: Module 1 has five SQLite business tools and no memory client or message_history. Browser bubbles are not model context. The local guardrails.py calls scope_turn and checked_reply; safety is present before memory is added. Customer, Billing case and Authorize selected refund for this message provide explicit per-turn scope; authorization resets each turn. PydanticAI’s prepare_refund exposes the write only when the customer, case and authorization are present. SQL checks policy, identity, amount and uniqueness. ReceiptGuard.run_once reuses saved request IDs. No escalation tool exists; service statuses are seeded examples. Source: module_1/app/agent.py; module_1/app/tools.py; module_1/app/guardrails.py; lib/operations.py. This diagram describes the architecture as memory is added. SQLite remains the system of record; module 1 uses only its business tools.

notes: Say — The selected case determines the current-turn scope. Show — Point to scope_turn(deps, policy_plan) and inspect the corresponding run. INSTRUCTIONS is the actual constructor prompt constant. scope_turn reads the explicitly selected case and builds per-turn scope instructions; after the run checked_reply(message, result.output, deps, scope) verifies action claims against receipts. The SQL write still validates the case, amount, current plan limit and uniqueness.

notes: Say — The four probes check fixture retrieval. Show — Show a pass with an accepted ID and an otherwise exact value with a missing ID marked failed. If blocked — Use the grader and a labeled example if no local scorecard is available.

notes: The package persists and retrieves memory; PydanticAI executes the model and tools. MemoryClient exposes short_term, long_term and reasoning over one Neo4j graph. Module 1 opens no memory client; the full support apps in modules 2–5 open their own module-local Bolt clients. Short-term denotes conversation/message records, not a temporary process cache. Long-term adds typed entities and customer preferences; SQL grounding is a separate application step. Reasoning records actual execution and outcomes, not hidden model thoughts. Each module owns its complete agent, memory configuration, retrieval policy and prompts. Hosted module-5 REST workflows are a separate optional service path.

notes: This is explicit integration, not an automatic Agent wrapper. A long-lived module-local MemoryClient stores records. Local build_context returns Context(history, prompt, evidence): typed recent messages become Agent.run(message_history=context.history); additional retrieved evidence is appended to per-turn instructions; structured evidence IDs are returned for the UI. Constructing a MemoryClient alone does not give an agent history. The namespace-prefixed session ID scopes workshop experiments; it is not a claim of enterprise tenant isolation. Retrieved evidence is not authority or current SQL policy. Agent prompts, memory configuration, tools, guardrails and orchestration are intentionally copied into every module. Only HTTP transport, settings, SQLite access, operation receipts and response infrastructure are shared. Read app/agent.py first; compare adjacent app folders to see the added concept.

notes: Say — The module reuses one connected client across turns. Show — Point to async with MemoryClient(config) and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Condensed from module_2/app/memory.py build_settings/open_memory. Imports: MemoryClient and MemorySettings from neo4j_agent_memory. AppSettings reads environment or .env; get_settings exports the configured OpenAI key for package clients. Database and bounded connection/retry settings are omitted only from the display. Pin: neo4j-agent-memory[pydantic-ai,openai]==0.8.0. Module 1 has no MemoryClient and uses OpenAI for chat only. The full support apps in modules 2–5 use module-local Bolt clients and OpenAI for chat and embeddings; modules 3–5 additionally configure LLM extraction. Module 2 sets extractor_type="none". Optional hosted NAMS REST workflows and the module-5 fresh skill consumer are separate paths. This example passes MemorySettings explicitly; backend is a settings field, not a MemoryClient constructor keyword.

notes: Module 2 writes user and assistant messages with short_term.add_message; the first write creates the Conversation. Local build_context returns Context(history, prompt, evidence). The newest ten prior messages are reversed into chronological order and converted by as_model_history: user → ModelRequest(UserPromptPart), assistant → ModelResponse(TextPart). Agent.run receives message_history=context.history. Namespace-wide semantic user messages (same or other conversations) go into instructions: cosine >=0.5, at most five after deduplication and recall-question-prefix filtering. Exclude the current message ID. Evidence preserves IDs and recent_conversation / semantic_message paths. The namespace convention is not enterprise tenant isolation. Source: module_2/app/context.py; module_2/app/agent.py; module_2/app/memory.py.

notes: Say — Both participants’ turns persist under the same session ID. Show — Point to short_term.add_message and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Normal persistence path from module_2/app/agent.py ChatService._turn. short_term is self.memory.short_term. The service prefixes session IDs with the workshop namespace. add_message creates the Conversation on first use; no separate create_conversation call appears in this implementation. The user flag is extract_entities=not self.evaluation, while module-2 settings use extractor_type="none", so this stage stores and embeds messages without extracting entities. Retain user_message.id to exclude the just-written message from history/retrieval. The assistant reply is checked against business receipts before persistence; persistence failures are surfaced as warnings. Database records survive process restarts, but the caller must reuse the session and namespace to restore that history.

notes: Say — Identify the inputs available to the model. Show — Have a learner point to the ID in history, semantic evidence, or both. If blocked — If the fact appears in both paths, accept both. The observed answer alone cannot attribute causation.

notes: Module 3 retains typed recent history and adds LLM extraction, SQL hydration, entities, preferences and model-selected memory tools. app/memory.py configures extractor_type=llm and disables automatic enrichment. ONTOLOGY selects acme_cloud, default-poleo or active; an explicit file wins. Only current-message mentions with type-compatible, exact unambiguous names/aliases get SQL facts. grounded_facts and lookup_facts validate; add_entity refreshes description and PropertyWriter sets flat fields. Inspect hydrated_from: a generated description alone is not SQL authority. Live semantic edges are RELATED_TO with the domain relation in the type property; UI/snapshot labels may show the logical name. Source: module_3/app/agent.py; context.py; hydrate.py; memory.py; ontology/acme_cloud.yaml.

notes: Say — Three experiments use different inputs and outputs. Show — Compare the fixed transcript, a live chat message and the validator fixture. If blocked — Select the named Saved replay for extraction-only results.

notes: Say — The message write can create MENTIONS edges. Show — Point to extract_entities=True and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Startup and normal-message-write fragments; the full app reuses one connected client across turns. Imports: MemoryClient and load_ontology from neo4j_agent_memory; build_settings from module_3/app/memory.py. The default ONTOLOGY=acme_cloud loads the local file; default-poleo loads the generic local file; active passes ontology=None and uses the database active version. An explicit file wins over that version. The actual user flag is extract_entities=not self.evaluation; evaluation skips extraction and hydration. add_message creates the conversation if necessary. Module 3 configures extractor_type="llm", enrichment.enabled=False and the selected validation mode. The app drops invalid relations; strict also filters undeclared entity types. Ontology node labels map POLE types/subtypes (for example PERSON/CUSTOMER) to display labels (Customer). Live extracted entity relations are stored as RELATED_TO with the ontology relation in its type property; the extractor-only Saved replay displays logical relation labels directly. Optional Wikimedia enrichment belongs to module_3/lab/enrichment.py and creates cached Saved replay data, not an automatic live-graph write.

notes: Say — Inspect grounded fields on the matched graph entity. Show — Point to writer.set_properties and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Excerpt from hydrate_session_entities after grounded_facts has returned a non-None result. The agent passes the current user message ID; only entities that message mentions are hydrated. Local lookup_facts performs parameterized SQLite reads. grounded_facts rejects conflicting exact-name/alias matches and incompatible POLE base types (PERSON for customers, OBJECT for products/plans, ORGANIZATION for organizations). The public long_term.add_entity upsert refreshes description; the pinned SDK does not refresh existing flat attributes, so a module-local PropertyWriter uses its own pooled Neo4j driver and opens a short session per write. memory.query.cypher is read-only. No _apply_flat_attributes or _lookup_hydration helper exists in this version. Existing resolved entity names remain unchanged (resolve=False, deduplicate=False). Inspect hydrated_from for SQL provenance; generated descriptions alone are not authoritative. A later mention refreshes facts after a SQL change; this is not automatic CDC. The local instructor plan fixture verifies Pro → Enterprise → Pro without modifying the live participant graph.

notes: Say — The agent can call the module-local memory tools. Show — Point to create_memory_tools(memory) and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Construction fragment from module_3/app/agent.py. create_memory_tools is local workshop code, not the package tool registry; it shares the familiar integration tool names but scopes queries to the workshop namespace/customer and records tool receipts. INSTRUCTIONS + SHORT_TERM_INSTRUCTIONS + LONG_TERM_INSTRUCTIONS are the actual constants. The short-term instructions teach evidence use; the long-term instructions request search_memory for account-history requests and save_preference when asked to store a preference. context.py retrieves before the model call; search_memory permits another query during the run. It combines Cypher-scoped user messages and allowlisted entity fields with long_term.get_preferences_for for the selected user. ToolDeps carries the explicitly selected customer, namespace, embedder and current_message_id. recall_preferences has no model-visible topic argument. SQL tools and module-local guardrails still validate current business facts and actions.

notes: Say — The lookup uses the selected customer’s user identifier. Show — Point to get_preferences_for and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Write-tool and retrieval-helper fragments. customer_id is a local helper returning f"{namespace}:{customer_email}". save_preference takes RunContext[ToolDeps], category, preference and optional context. It returns needs_customer before the shown block if no customer is selected. The SDK deduplicates similar preferences within a category across users, so the category is also prefixed with the customer identifier. user_identifier creates (:User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE]->(:Preference). The receipt uses stored.id/category/preference/context and stored.metadata.get("deduplicated", False); it reports what the SDK actually stored. Retrieval calls the public long_term.get_preferences_for API rather than category-prefix Cypher. search_preferences returns at most ten customer_preference evidence rows and returns an empty list if no customer is selected. The model tool recall_preferences() takes no topic argument. No preference automatically authorizes a business action. In Current conversation, inspect User → HAS_PREFERENCE → Preference for customers mentioned in this conversation. Use All stored memory for the broader graph. The selected customer scopes the tool’s save and recall.

notes: Say — The learner should point to a concrete source and field. Show — Ask which Message mentions the entity and which customer field SQLite supplies. If blocked — Accept missing or variable extraction this run and ask where to inspect the evidence.

notes: Module 4 opens a ReasoningTrace before scope checks and model execution. After reply persistence, record_execution records collected tools and server guards, then attempts completion even on failure. ReasoningTrace HAS_STEP ReasoningStep USES_TOOL ToolCall INSTANCE_OF Tool. Trace INITIATED_BY Message; Step TOUCHED explicit case Customer/Plan; ToolCall can be TRIGGERED_BY Message. TOUCHED carries the selected case context on each collected call. Inspect the operation result, captured SQL and action receipt to establish what the call did. Error priority is recording failure, execution_error, policy_declined, then none. similar_executions retrieves only completed traces in the selected namespace, cosine >=0.45 and at most three; declined traces are eligible. The current open trace is excluded. Source: module_4/app/agent.py; reasoning.py; memory_tools.py.

notes: Say — TOUCHED records the selected case context. Show — Follow Trace → Step → ToolCall. Read captured SQL and operation result to support any action claim. If blocked — Use the dated saved replay and distinguish it from the live graph.

notes: Say — A trace exists before the current model execution. Show — Point to start_trace and inspect the corresponding run. The code reference shows the surrounding setup, use of role-preserving history, and later completion in record_execution. Inspect a recorded run to observe the trace ID.

notes: Say — Each captured call receives the selected case context. Show — Point to touched_entities=refs and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. record_execution computes case references once, then passes the same list with every collected call. Follow INITIATED_BY to the initiating message. TOUCHED describes case context. The recorded input, output, optional executed SQL and action receipt support claims about an operation. Each step keeps its own result.

notes: Say — A completed trace records execution and business status. Show — Point to complete_trace and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Imports: TraceOutcome from neo4j_agent_memory.schema.models and json. Condensed from module_4/app/reasoning.py:107–164. status = business_status(tool_calls) selects the latest issue_refund/refund_policy_guard receipt or no_action. declined means status starts with rejected or equals requires_confirmation. error_kind precedence is recording exception name, execution_error when execution_ok=False, policy_declined, then None. Real code constructs TraceOutcome inside complete_trace; named outcome is presentation-only factoring. The real outcome includes related_entities=refs and metrics execution_succeeded/tool_calls, with no unmeasured policy_compliant assertion. Exact checked reply is retained as JSON. finally attempts completion after execution or recording failure; outages can still prevent storage.

notes: Module 4 opens a ReasoningTrace before scope checks and model execution. After reply persistence, record_execution records collected tools and server guards, then attempts completion even on failure. ReasoningTrace HAS_STEP ReasoningStep USES_TOOL ToolCall INSTANCE_OF Tool. Trace INITIATED_BY Message; Step TOUCHED explicit case Customer/Plan; ToolCall can be TRIGGERED_BY Message. TOUCHED carries the selected case context on each collected call. Inspect the operation result, captured SQL and action receipt to establish what the call did. Error priority is recording failure, execution_error, policy_declined, then none. similar_executions retrieves only completed traces in the selected namespace, cosine >=0.45 and at most three; declined traces are eligible. The current open trace is excluded. Source: module_4/app/agent.py; reasoning.py; memory_tools.py. The reasoning_retrieval toggle disables pre-turn examples and mid-turn search_memory procedures; by itself it still records new traces. The controlled make s4-refund-repeat runner additionally sets evaluation=True and record_reasoning=False in both branches: no extraction, hydration or branch trace writes. It uses identical private SQLite copies, separate message scopes and one frozen declined-refund corpus. Compare saved hashes, evidence, tools, tokens, timing and policy compliance. A benefit is not guaranteed. The fixture is module_4/lab/ablation.py; orchestration is scripts/run_scenario.py.

notes: Say — A matched past trace supplies steps and tool results. Show — Point to get_trace_with_steps and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Imports: UUID from uuid and local similar_executions. Three scopes: first block inside similar_executions; middle inside ChatService._recall_executions; final block in ChatService._turn. Source: module_4/app/reasoning.py:36–92 and agent.py:187–195,259–271. Namespace Cypher requires completed_at IS NOT NULL before ranking, excluding the trace opened for this turn. It checks task_embedding and selects up to three cosine matches ≥0.45, including completed declines. get_trace_with_steps supplies actual steps, tool arguments/results and outcome; as_example serializes them, and trace IDs join context.evidence. _turn injects nonempty examples labeled Past execution examples (not current policy). SDK get_similar_traces uses global top-k; local query provides exact namespace isolation. reasoning_retrieval=False disables both pre-turn and search_memory procedure retrieval but alone still records traces. The controlled make s4-refund-repeat runner additionally sets record_reasoning=False and evaluation=True in both branches: no branch traces, extraction or hydration; identical private SQL copies, separate message namespaces and one fixed corpus seeded by module_4/lab/ablation.py. Identical outcomes are valid. Retrieval errors surface warnings without necessarily failing the turn.

If blocked — At workshop minute 130 take off/fallback. Use remaining time for evidence and debrief. Use a labeled previous result only if it exists.

notes: Memory supplies context, entity knowledge and recorded actions/outcomes. A distillation run selects evidence and derives a portable procedure with conditions and source links. A receiving agent supplies its own tools and authorization and checks current business policy. Grounding is evidence for inspection, not proof of correctness or suitability. No new memory type is introduced. Distillation changes an instruction artifact, not model weights. A raw trace records one execution; a skill generalizes a reusable procedure, while the receiving agent performs a new execution. The workshop fixture is canonical authored history rather than a recording uploaded from the participant app. The module 5 support app retains the full module 4 Bolt/AuraDB memory behavior. Hosted REST workflows seed canonical authored fixtures into a separate NAMS workspace; they do not migrate participant AuraDB data. Skill distillation builds a reusable procedure on top of memory, not a fourth memory store or model-weight training. Source: module_5/app/agent.py; module_5/app/memory.py; module_5/workflows/*.py. References · checked 2026-11-04 Skill concepts: https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/explanation/skills/ Skills API: https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/reference/skills-api/

notes: Memory supplies context, entity knowledge and recorded actions/outcomes. A distillation run selects evidence and derives a portable procedure with conditions and source links. A receiving agent supplies its own tools and authorization and checks current business policy. Grounding is evidence for inspection, not proof of correctness or suitability. Diagram: selected memory feeds a scoped distillation run; after succeeded the workshop approves, publishes and downloads a versioned package. Fresh agent loads SKILL.md and calls business tools. Approval is submitted automatically by this script; it does not stop for human review. Failed/error/cancelled runs or timeout lead to explicit fallback guidance. Three memory types remain the input foundation. Diagram detail: Conceptual application pipeline: three existing memory types provide persisted evidence; scope selects relevant evidence, distillation abstracts a procedure, review/package creates a portable versioned artifact, fresh agent consumes the file with current business tools. No edges between foundation nodes are asserted here. Process arrows are not database relationships. No model fine-tuning occurs. Workshop review submission is automated; a production human decision requires a separate policy/workflow. References · checked 2026-11-04 Skill concepts: https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/explanation/skills/ Skills API: https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/reference/skills-api/

notes: distill.py downloads the generated version, stages its files, checks SKILL.md and the run in provenance.json, and installs the package with skill.json. That receipt records skillId, versionId, runId and the seed conversationId. Fresh-agent consumption reads only SKILL.md; it does not automatically ingest supporting files or verify attestation. Current service deployment determines optional package/attestation fields. Reruns reuse the named skill through skillId and publish a new version. notes: Say — The graph represents SkillStep grounding and the package records claims. Show — Locate a grounded step in the NAMS graph, then compare a real groundedIn ID in provenance.json. If blocked — Use this task only with a hosted package. Fallback pairs go directly to the wrap.

notes: Say — Grounding and coverage are signals for review. Show — Ask which contrasting cases the two $49 successful fixtures omit. If blocked — Use the seeded source code to identify the case distribution, clearly labeling it as fixture inspection.

notes: Say — A fresh agent receives the downloaded procedure as instructions. Show — Point to load_skill("on") and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Imports: Agent from pydantic_ai; INSTRUCTIONS from local app.agent; SQLITE_TOOLS and ToolDeps from local tools. Combines load_skill, create_fresh_agent construction and run_fresh_agent for explicit on mode; real create_fresh_agent appends the heading only if skill is not None. Adjacent literals reproduce the exact heading. Current source: module_5/app/fresh_agent.py:32–85. on requires artifacts/distilled/SKILL.md; fallback explicitly uses artifacts/pre-distilled-skill/SKILL.md; off has no skill. Missing on artifact raises rather than silently becoming a control. run_fresh_agent uses a temporary SQLite copy and clears the Ravi duplicate-compute refund only in that copy, so off/on start from the same open case and the workshop database stays unchanged. ToolDeps supplies Ravi’s account, incident_id and explicit authorization. This direct model demo skips scope_turn/checked_reply and returns model output; issue_refund retains SQL validation. No MemoryClient, message_history or search_memory is installed. One command runs one mode: compare make s5-fresh-agent WITH_SKILL=off and WITH_SKILL=on. Use WITH_SKILL=fallback deliberately for the checked-in fixture. Fewer calls or better outcomes are not guaranteed. The downloaded ZIP also contains references/ and provenance.json, but the receiving agent loads only SKILL.md. Skill distillation transfers an instruction artifact; it does not update model weights.

notes: Say — Ravi’s $49 case runs on a fresh private SQL copy in both arms. Show — Run off, then on for an available hosted package, or fallback for the checked-in procedure. Compare the ordered names, optional returned statuses and reply. If blocked — If capabilities are disabled or there is no package at minute five, use off/fallback and go to the wrap. If a model run also fails, label any archived output explicitly. The consumer loads only SKILL.md and its local SQL tools. It has no history or memory client. Each run receives explicit case authorization. Off/on can produce the same action.

notes: Say — SQLite policy, hosted drift, and a new skill version are three different observations. Show — Check the SQL change, returned staleClaims and staleSteps, and the procedure and provenance diff for the same skill. If blocked — Use a labeled recorded example or skip this extension. Fallback participants continue directly from their consumer comparison to the wrap.

notes: Say — The report identifies stale claims and steps for this skill. Show — Point to /drift and inspect the corresponding run. If blocked — Use this panel for code reference, then return to the live scenario. Code reference for the optional hosted route. Use the direct off/fallback comparison if the package is unavailable at minute five. Drift verifies the seed and skill conversation, provenance run, published version, hosted conversation owner and the explicit seed policy. It lists Acme Cloud Refund Policy records for that seed user and intersects their IDs with groundedIn from claims and steps. Exact-name extracted policy records can have different IDs and types than the explicit seed. Only cited matches are eligible. If none qualify, stop. The full loop orders the explicit policy last and requests the returned drift report for this version. Use a disposable workspace. Older packages can still supply SKILL.md for a fresh consumer.

notes: Say — Three observations represent three different state changes. Show — Point to the before/after SQL values, returned drift fields, and version diff. If blocked — Use a labeled archived example when present. Skip hosted drift in the consumption-only fallback.

notes: Say — This is an instructor-led destructive demonstration on disposable hosted records. Show — Check the workspace and provenance target IDs, read every printed before/after value, and stop once the SQL default is restored. If blocked — Skip writes if workspace, skill or starting state cannot be verified. Use a supplied recorded example explicitly labeled as such. November 4 rehearsal: changing SQLite alone left the hosted version current. Removing two cited, exact-name extracted policies in the seed user’s scope left 2/5 claims and 1/3 steps stale. The new version still described $250 when local SQL held $150. Compare the returned values from your run.

A single accepted ID qualifies even when other supplied IDs are irrelevant. If blocked — Use the labeled example and show scripts/eval.py when a run is unavailable.

No cross-backend graph edges are created. Controlled eval checks exact facts plus accepted source IDs using private SQL and unique namespaces with business tools disabled. It is a retrieval probe, not an overall support-quality grade. The UI loads saved results for the current module; opening it does not invoke a model.
